summary: Steamboat Mountain's 1928 cabin gave way to a 1956 R-6 timber tower, staffed to about 1965 and gone by 1966; four corner blocks remain in the summit area.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab on a 20-foot treated timber tower (1956); earlier 14-by-14-foot cabin (1928)
facts.status_note: Tower removed by 1966, by burning according to Will Hite and the Washington lookouts page, or torn down according to Oregon Hikers; four corner blocks remain in the summit area

access.note: Easy trail; Will Hite gives the hike distance as 3/4 mile and says the trail climbs 600 feet from the parking area; gravel-road trailhead in the Indian Heaven Wilderness

visit.trail_note: Hike distance 3/4 mile per Will Hite; trail climbs 600 feet from the parking area; the trailhead sits at a huge quarry reached by gravel road

events.note: 14-by-14-foot cabin built per the register and FireLookout.com; Will Hite dates a cathedral-style lookout to 1928
Washington lookouts page dates a cathedral-style lookout house to 1930, citing a January 1931 newspaper item
Cabin replaced by a 20-foot treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab
Forest supervisor said Steamboat would be the only manned lookout in the Mt. Adams district; six of 37 forest lookouts to be manned
Register says still staffed in 1965; FireLookout.com says photos from 1964 and 1965 show it being staffed
Gone by 1966; Will Hite says removed by burning; Washington lookouts page says removed by burning in the mid-1960s; Oregon Hikers says torn down
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on July 18, 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, FireLookout.com and Will Hite date the first lookout to 1928; the Washington lookouts page dates a cathedral-style house to 1930 and cites a January 1931 story. Not resolved; the story gives both.

Will Hite and the Washington lookouts page say the tower was removed by burning (by 1966, or in the mid-1960s); Oregon Hikers says it was torn down after standing about ten years. The sources do not reconcile the method, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The brief's design R-6 is confirmed for the 1956 tower; the design field now also gives the 1928 cabin. The 1928 vs 1930 build date and the burned vs torn-down fate are unresolved across sources. The Oregon Hikers page is a hiking guide rather than a historical source, so its fate claim is reported as its own view. No new photos found. Brief status gone and FFLOS date confirmed.
